reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
For this item, you have been given a cardboard ruler. If you do not have the cardboard ruler raise your hand. Use the map below and your ruler to answer this set of questions.

Marytown is a new town. The people of Marytown are planning their new town. They decided to put the town hall halfway between the lake and the forest, as shown on the map below. They made their measurements from the X's.

Marytown

[Image: Map of Marytown]

Add a park, a library, and a school to the map of Marytown using the following information.

B. The library should be at least 300 meters but no more than 400 meters from the town hall. On the map, mark with an X where you would put the library and write library below the X.

descriptors: Library between 2.8 cm and 4.2 cm from town hall, measured from X to X
Library less than 2.8 cm from town hall, measured from X to X
Library more than 4.2 cm from town hall, measured from X to X
Other incorrect (including crossed out/erased, stray marks, illegible, or off task)

reference_items.scoring_notes: Note: Park and library need not to be in a straight line.
reference_items.figure_description:
A map of Marytown enclosed in an irregular rectangular border.
Near the top right inside the border, text states: "Scale: 1 cm represents 100 meters".
In the upper-left quadrant is a forest represented by a cluster of pine trees, with an "X" mark below it labeled "Forest".
Near the center of the map is an "X" mark labeled "Town Hall" below it.
In the lower-right quadrant is an outlined body of water with wavy horizontal lines inside, with an "X" mark directly above it labeled "Lake".
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2003 data, 2007 bridging data, and 2007 data (fourth-grade mathematics).

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
Class A and B each have 40 students.

[Image: Pie chart for Class A and bar graph for Class B]

There are more girls in Class A than in Class B. How many more?
reference_items.figure_description:
Two graphs representing student populations in Class A and Class B:
- On the left, a pie chart titled "Class A" showing a circle divided into two sectors. An unshaded sector representing one quarter of the circle (from 9 o'clock to 12 o'clock) is labeled "Boys". The remaining three-quarters of the circle is shaded grey and labeled "Girls".
- On the right, a bar graph titled "Class B" with a vertical axis labeled with values from 0 to 24 in increments of 4 (0, 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24) with horizontal grid lines. The horizontal axis has two categories: "Boys", with a light-grey bar of height 24, and "Girls", with a dark bar of height 16.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2003 data, 2007 bridging data, and 2007 data (fourth-grade mathematics).

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
This chart shows the types of cookies sold by the local bakery.

[Image: Pie chart titled Cookies Sold, shaded and divided into various sizes; sugar about one-fourth, chocolate chip more than one-fourth, oatmeal more than one-half, and vanilla about one-eighth.]

Which type of cookie did the bakery sell the most of?
reference_items.figure_description:
A pie chart titled "Cookies Sold" is divided into four unequal sectors:
- "sugar": light-gray shading, occupying the top-right quadrant from the 12 o'clock position to the 3 o'clock position (a right angle, exactly one-quarter of the circle).
- "chocolate chip": medium-gray shading, occupying the sector from the 3 o'clock position to approximately the 5 o'clock position.
- "oatmeal": white (unshaded), occupying the largest sector from approximately the 5 o'clock position counter-clockwise around the bottom and left to approximately the 10:30 position.
- "vanilla": white (unshaded), occupying the sector from approximately the 10:30 position to the 12 o'clock position.
Visually, oatmeal is the largest sector, sugar is the second largest, chocolate chip is third, and vanilla is the smallest.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2007 and 2011 fourth-grade mathematics data.

slope.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the two-parameter logistic (2PL) model, which TIMSS uses for constructed-response items worth 1 point, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1995 and 2003 fourth-grade mathematics data". What is the item's slope (discrimination) parameter a? A higher a means that the item separates students of lower and higher mathematics ability more sharply. Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration. Use them to place this item.
